    c.domain_id,
    c.vocabulary_id

    AND c.vocabulary_id = 'RxNorm'
    AND c.standard_concept = 'S'

Sin embargo, omite por completo la lógica crucial para determinar si un medicamento es 'monocomponente' (es decir, que contiene un único principio activo). He revisado y mejorado la consulta SQL para BigQuery, incorporando la lógica necesaria para asegurar que solo se seleccionen los medicamentos que contienen **exactamente un** principio activo (monocomponente), y que este sea 'Ondansetrón' (Concept ID 1000560).

Aquí tienes la consulta SQL corregida:

args.sql_query:
SELECT
    c.concept_id,
    c.concept_name,
    c.domain_id,
    c.vocabulary_id
FROM
    concept AS c
JOIN
    concept_ancestor AS ca
    ON c.concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
WHERE
    ca.ancestor_concept_id = 1000560 -- Concepto de ingrediente "Ondansetron"
    AND c.domain_id = 'Drug'
    AND c.vocabulary_id = 'RxNorm'
    AND c.standard_concept = 'S'
    AND c.concept_id IN (
        SELECT
            cr.concept_id_1
        FROM
            concept_relationship AS cr
        JOIN
            concept AS c_ing
            ON cr.concept_id_2 = c_ing.concept_id
        WHERE
            cr.relationship_id = 'Has ingredient'
            AND c_ing.domain_id = 'Drug' -- Asegura que el concepto relacionado es un fármaco/ingrediente
            AND c_ing.standard_concept = 'S'
        GROUP BY
            cr.concept_id_1
        HAVING
            COUNT(DISTINCT cr.concept_id_2) = 1
    )
